about: Every field generator in materials/wgsl-field.ts, and the §9.1 material it is supposed to implement.
Enforced by web/tools/artcheck.mjs, which REPLACES rulecheck rule 9.0 — a word-grep that returned
PASS on a science-fiction generator for two days because the code used the removed spec own vocabulary.
A static gate cannot decide whether geometry matches an art direction. This one decides whether anyone
has LOOKED, and whether the generator has changed since they did. The bodySha is the load-bearing part:
an art-direction change can land in the contract and in sets.ts while a generator is never touched,
and nothing would catch it. Editing a generator breaks the gate until someone re-reads it.
To review one: read the generator against ARCHITECTURE.md §9.0/§9.1, replace UNREVIEWED with what it
actually implements, set verdict to OK or VIOLATION, stamp reviewedBy/reviewedAt, then run
This file starts almost entirely UNREVIEWED because that is the truth. Fabricating sixteen
justifications to make the gate green would be the same lie rule 9.0 was telling.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded earth. Worley clods with a domed profile, pebbles turned up through them, fine grain, and crevices between clods. A moisture channel modulated by wearBias, so it darkens and weathers rather than staying pristine. No emissive, nothing invented.
generators.note: Read in full 2026-07-30 while chasing 0.1b. Contributes 5.152% of albedo variance and 14.735% of the lighting denominator.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Dryness derived from the field moisture, raised on convexity because high spots dry first and lowered by occlusion because hollows stay wet. Roughness interpolates between the wet and dry tints’ OWN roughness values. metal 0, no emissive.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded geology. Ridged mass, sedimentary bedding planes, a worley joint/fracture network, and grit. A stain channel modulated by wearBias. This is real rock behaviour, not invented material.
generators.note: Read in full 2026-07-30. It carries 33.923% of the LIGHTING denominator — the largest share of any surface — and only 6.780% of albedo variance. heightScale 0.55 is the highest of all sets, which is WHY it carries the shading signal. Do not reduce it.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Iron staining follows OCCLUSION rather than noise — "iron leaches DOWN out of the joints" — and polish follows convexity, so exposed faces smooth and crevices stain. Correct geology in both directions. metal 0.
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-07-30. Carries 33.923% of the lighting denominator, the largest of any surface.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded sand. Dunes carrying wind ripples that thin out on the LEE side — real aeolian behaviour rather than uniform corrugation. packed channel on wearBias.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. Contributes 0.047%% of albedo variance, the least of any surface.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Damp from occlusion plus concavity minus the field dryness, so sand is wet in hollows. A sparse mineral speckle from its own value noise. metal 0.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded gravel. Worley stones at two scales — bed stones and chips — with dust between them, fine grit, and cavity in the gaps. A dry channel modulated by wearBias. Real crushed stone.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30 while checking the 0.1b palette lever. Carries 18.367%% of the lighting denominator from only 0.14 m of relief, because worley pebbles give high-frequency normals at low amplitude.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Every stone takes its own tone from its own cell hash, with the source note that "a single grey rubble field is the tell that a gravel texture was painted rather than grown". Dust fill from occlusion and cavity. metal 0.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded grass. Worley tufts modulated by a density field, blades combing along a noise-lattice direction so layer variants differ, fine detail, and a matId marking bare soil showing through thin patches. A dryness channel modulated by wearBias, so it browns and weathers.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. Its "lattice direction" is the NOISE lattice, not the Lattice faction — checked, because that word appears in both senses in this codebase and confusing them would have produced a false art-direction flag. Its tintA luminance is 0.075, the darkest non-ash surface and darker than wet grass, which is why it is the largest single target of the 0.1b palette lever.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Dryness from the field with convexity, then a direct occlusion multiply because "blade tips catch the light; the base of a tuft is deeply occluded and darker". Bare-soil matId swaps to the third tint. metal 0.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded asphalt. Aggregate in bitumen, polished wheel bands, and a crack network that is SUPPRESSED under the wheel path because traffic seals it — a real behaviour, not a texture trick. Repair patches. wear channel on wearBias.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. The crack term is multiplied by (1 - wheel*0.6), which is why the road reads as used rather than merely cracked.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. The wheel band is POLISHED, not dirtied — "the aggregate is worn flat, so it is SMOOTHER than the untravelled bitumen either side of it". Cracks darken, repairs tint, roughness follows the polish. Most people get this one backwards. metal 0.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded industrial plate. Staggered plating with rivet runs, DIRECTIONAL brushing (explicitly not isotropic noise), dents, and rust nucleating out of the seams via rustSeed at full wearBias. Hazard chevrons are painted rather than formed, so they barely lift.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. Carries a §9 note in the source worth keeping: the chevron band is kept NARROW because a third of the surface in team paint would read as a hue shift over the whole material rather than as a marking. The author was reasoning about art direction correctly here.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Oxide blooms out of seams and sheltered pockets where water sits; bare steel survives on proud lips. Two notes worth keeping: metalness is 0 or 1 with a SPATIAL transition, because "paint and oxide are dielectric films over the plate; a fractional metalness is not a material, it is a mistake"; and the paint mask thresholds rather than multiplies its wear terms, because "a mask that only ever reaches 0.88 desaturates every player colour on the map by 12%".
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-07-30. The second note is a measured consequence, not a preference.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded concrete. Poured against board forms that leave a regular course of shallow lines with tie-holes, spalled back to exposed aggregate at the edges, crack network, grit. age channel on wearBias.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. Board-form marks and spalling are both real construction artefacts.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Weathering from field age, occlusion and concavity; chalking on convex faces; exposed aggregate and cracks take their own tints. A painted apron band laid across the slab rather than following the noise, and it loses the mask as weathering rises. metal 0.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded water. Two crossed wave trains plus chop and fine detail; height carries almost everything because deep water is nearly pure normal and reflectance. foam channel on wearBias.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. Returns cav 0 and sub 0 deliberately — deep water has no cavity or sub-material.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Deliberately almost all specular: "the albedo floor exists only so the §7 range holds, and the visual work is done by the normal and a very low roughness". Foam on convex crests scaled by the field. ao forced to 1 — deep water has no cavity.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded shallows. A visible bed under a thin ripple: bedded stones, silt fill, surface ripple, and a depth field reduced where stone stands proud. Real river-bed behaviour.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. The bed reads THROUGH, tinted by how much water covers it, because "that depth cue is what separates shallow from deep at a glance, and it must not be a flat overlay". ao lifts toward 1 with depth. metal 0.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded snow. Drift (fbm), sastrugi (wind-carved ridges — a real snow feature, not invented), a worley crust with broken patches, and a fine sparkle band. The fresh channel is modulated by wearBias so it weathers rather than staying pristine. No emissive, no invented material. This generator is FINE.
generators.note: Read in full 2026-07-30 while chasing 0.1b, where snow is 77.458% of the albedo variance. That variance is NOT this generator: it produces the field (height/density/cavity/matId), and the albedo comes from the set tints in sets.ts. See issues/gfx-1.md 0.1b.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Shading is almost entirely occlusion: "crevices go blue because the sky is all that reaches them, so the blue is driven by the derived AO, never painted in". Physically exact, and the reason snow reads flat at heightScale 0.20 — with a near-uniform 0.82 albedo, occlusion is its ONLY source of form.
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-07-30. This is the mechanism behind the deferred lever 2 in gfx-1 0.1b.

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded ash fall. Fine fall with a shrinkage-crack network, crust flakes, and powder. The heat channel is EMBERS, which §9.0 explicitly permits — fire and embers are on its allowed-emissive list — and it is deliberately low frequency because heat survives in pockets rather than per grain.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. The one generator with a legitimately emissive-adjacent channel, and it is permitted by name in §9.0 rather than by exception.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. The ember glow is gated on occlusion AND on being inside a crack, because "ember light on an exposed flake would be nonsense". §9.0 permits fire and embers by name, so this is allowed emissive correctly constrained rather than an exception. metal 0.
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-07-30. The only surface with a legitimately emissive-adjacent channel.

generators.implements: Faceted crystal grown out of a dull matrix with sharp arrises and a metallic vein — real mineralogy (quartz and pyrite veins in dull rock), and harvestable ore as crystal is RTS genre convention rather than science fiction. The facet is a PLANE across the worley cell rather than a dome, which is what gives a crystal its hard arris under light. Produces no emissive.
generators.note: Reviewed 2026-07-30. ONE NAMING SMELL worth fixing but not a violation: the density channel is called charge, which reads as energy. It behaves as a density/quality field (0.4 + 0.6*cell.z + wearBias*0.2) and drives sheen, not light. Rename it to grade or purity so nobody later reads charge as licence for a glow. Contributes only 1.992%% of albedo variance. Also carries a recorded seam fix: keying the facet tilt to the tile fraction instead of the cell frame put a hard step on every ninth column, which the seam probe caught as a 3x discontinuity.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Facet, matrix and vein take separate tints; the facet arris POLISHES rather than dulls because a crystal edge catches light. And the sci-fi concern is closed in the source: "only the vein is metal. The crystal is a dielectric and must not read as chrome."
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-07-30. Its density channel is still named `charge`, which reads as energy though it drives sheen — rename to `grade` or `purity`.

generators.implements: §9.1 Foundry: heavy cast and welded steel. Overlapping plate courses each sitting proud of its neighbour by a lip, continuous weld beads along the horizontal courses, rivet heads at the uprights, mill scale, and a painted stencil band raised only by its own paint film. Soot has a broad field whose DEPOSITION is decided in the shading pass by how enclosed the geometry actually is. wearBias enters the soot channel at full weight.
generators.note: EXEMPLARY, and it is the template the fieldLattice rewrite should follow. Every element is a real manufacturing fact rather than a texture idea: plates overlap because rolled plate does, courses are welded and uprights bolted because that is how it is built, soot settles where air is still. Read in full 2026-07-30.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Ochre wears through to steel on proud lips and rivet crowns, soot lands where the plate work encloses, and "both come out of the generated relief, not a decal". A weld bead is forced to the roughest bare steel on the hull because it is rippled and scaled. Player colour lands on whole plates with the panel boundary exactly at the plate boundary. || AMENDED 2026-08-05 (claude): player-colour mask coverage reduced toward §9.1's "a real repaint of specific panels and markings". The mask MECHANISM was measured correct first and wrongly suspected before that — read back off the baked r8 texture, Foundry matched its nominal coverage to within a point, bimodal exactly as authored. The NUMBER was the problem. Foundry face plates 38% -> ~20% (measured whole-texture 39.0% -> 31.4%; the difference is the stencil band, which is a MARKING and stays per §9.1). Lattice infill 26% -> ~14% (measured 25.0% -> 11.3%), window narrowed rather than shifted so the same panels stay painted and baselines do not churn for no design reason. No change to which materials exist, only how much of them is repainted. || AMENDED 2026-08-05 (codex): albedo alpha carries the constant 0.25 Foundry emitter class, not a filtered spatial mask. The forward path combines it with a unit-mesh-only analytic placement, so structures sharing the set remain dark. One warm-amber status strip is permitted by §9.0 as a real alive/ownership indicator; no seam, trim, or decorative panel glows.
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-08-05 after stage-1 emissive. The constant set tag cannot repeat or mip into broad emission; measured placement is 1.875% of eligible body pixels and 4.423x the Foundry lit hull.

generators.implements: §9.1 Lattice: open field-bolted framework built from angle-iron plate boundaries and alternating diagonal girder flanges, with triangular gusset plates at every node and denser washer/bolt runs than Foundry. Infill alternates real corrugated galvanised sheet and sun-faded canvas: sheet screws land in dimples along corrugation crowns; canvas is hemmed and laced through metal eyelets. Zinc has crystalline spangle and blooms to rough white chalk; olive paint frets from exposed frame edges; steel rusts from fasteners and sheltered joins; canvas loses pigment on exposed faces. No trace, ceramic, hex panel or no-corrosion path remains.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 v2 / §9.1 v2 (2026-08-05). Anodised pale alloy over a bolted alloy frame. The field relief is UNCHANGED and still v2-correct — bolted truss members, gusset plates and ribbed infill are exactly the v2 vocabulary. The material on it was rewritten: the zinc-bloom chalk term and the joint-rust term are DELETED, because §9.0 v2 puts corrosion above the wear ceiling and assigns it to drift and to damage states. matId 4/5 are reinterpreted from canvas and lacing cord to a composite infill panel and its recessed seam — identical geometry, so no field-pass regeneration. Wear is now settled dust in shelter (~1/3 the amplitude of the chalk it replaces) plus thin sun-facing decal fade, which sits inside the band rather than on its floor. Anodising and composite are dielectric films, so only the exposed machined flange and bare sheet read as metal, and the transition stays spatial. || AMENDED 2026-08-05 (claude): player-colour mask coverage reduced toward §9.1's "a real repaint of specific panels and markings". The mask MECHANISM was measured correct first and wrongly suspected before that — read back off the baked r8 texture, Lattice matched its nominal coverage to within a point, bimodal exactly as authored. The NUMBER was the problem. Foundry face plates 38% -> ~20% (measured whole-texture 39.0% -> 31.4%; the difference is the stencil band, which is a MARKING and stays per §9.1). Lattice infill 26% -> ~14% (measured 25.0% -> 11.3%), window narrowed rather than shifted so the same panels stay painted and baselines do not churn for no design reason. No change to which materials exist, only how much of them is repainted. || AMENDED 2026-08-05 (codex): albedo alpha carries the constant 0.75 Lattice emitter class, not a filtered spatial mask. The forward path combines it with a unit-mesh-only analytic placement, so structures sharing the set remain dark. One cool cyan-white status strip is permitted by §9.0 as a real alive/ownership indicator; no seam, trim, or decorative panel glows.
generators.shadeNote: Read 2026-08-05 after stage-1 emissive. The constant set tag cannot repeat or mip into broad emission; measured placement is 1.875% of eligible body pixels and 4.694x the Lattice lit hull.
generators.note: Rewritten twice. 2026-07-30 by codex against §9.0 v1; MATERIAL half rewritten 2026-08-05 by claude against §9.0 v2, which amended the wear rule from a floor to a band with a ceiling and moved canvas out of the Lattice palette. The v1 review was VALID when made and became stale when the standard moved — which nothing detected, because the inventory recorded no art-direction version. That hole is now closed by artcheck reviewedAgainst. Structural helper plateLattice is unchanged; hexLattice remains deleted. Side-by-side evidence predates v2 and must be recaptured: web/.artifacts/art-1/foundry-left_lattice-right.png

generators.implements: §9.0 grounded salvage. Large regions of mismatched material fastened together and abandoned: rusted plate, bleached panel, bare corroded metal, board, fastener. Bolts through plate regions, boards across their own region, corrugation across the plate regions, pitting corrosion, and decay at FULL wearBias.
generators.note: EXEMPLARY, and a SECOND template for the fieldLattice rewrite — arguably closer than fieldFoundry. It already implements corrugated sheet, visible bolts, boards and heavy weathering, which is exactly §9.1 open bolted framework vocabulary. The rewrite can borrow from here directly. Read in full 2026-07-30.
generators.shadeImplements: §9.0 grounded. Four salvaged materials chosen per region, each ageing its own way, with the intent stated: "the mismatch is the point: Drift exists to give the lighting something unowned". UV bleaches pigment from exposed faces first; a bolt head stays bright where it is proud; metalness steps per region. mask forced to 0 because "Drift is unowned, so it never carries a player’s colour".

greebles.implements: §9.1 Foundry geometry: bsp panels with a POSITIVE plateHeight so plate sits proud of the frame, hatches, vents, seams standing in for weld beads, and rivets. Real mass-produced steel construction.
greebles.note: Read in full 2026-07-30. Its rivets use sides: 6 — that is a HEXAGONAL BOLT HEAD, real hardware, and must not be confused with the removed hex PANELLING. A naive scan for the word hex would flag this wrongly, which is one more reason a word-grep cannot decide this question. Also carries a budget note worth keeping: per-pass budgets are explicit because greeble() spends the shared budget in pass order, and rivets are last — the faction whole read would otherwise be starved by the first pass.

greebles.implements: §9.1 Lattice geometry: bsp panels with a POSITIVE plateHeight so bolted-on sheet sits proud of its frame, a hatch bolted shut with six fasteners, angle-iron edging along the frame members rather than the Foundry weld beads, and rivet runs at 0.13 spacing — denser than Foundry 0.2, because §9.1 contrast is solid cast mass against OPEN BOLTED FRAMEWORK and this faction should show more hardware, not none. Wear raised above Foundry: zinc chalks, canvas frays, steel rusts at every fastener.
greebles.note: REWRITTEN 2026-07-30, previously a VIOLATION. It implemented the superseded spec in five separate decisions — hex tiling, negative plateHeight sinking tiles under a raised frame, fasteners: 0, seams: null and rivets: null — and survived the 2026-07-28 change because nothing scanned geo/. It was the FOURTH place that direction persisted. sides: 6 on the rivets is a hexagonal BOLT HEAD, real hardware, and not the hex PANELLING this preset used to generate. See issues/art-1.md.
